story.title: An opening in two directions
story.letter: The compass has opened a small hinge in its case. The kite has changed the edge of its sail. Let these two small departures begin another envelope.
story.goal: Make and send Compass Hinge and Tailwind.
story.sentCaption: The hinge and the altered sail went out together.

story.title: A draft across the table
story.letter: The kite stretches across its spar, with a second sail fragment at the far end. Give that broad crossing the small Compass Hinge for company.
story.goal: Make and send Compass Hinge and Cross Draft.
story.sentCaption: The cross draft found its small hinge.

story.title: A bearing left open
story.letter: An open triangle interrupts the compass face. Tailwind keeps its own smaller cut in the sail. This reply can wait while you finish the other direction.
story.goal: Make and send Off North and Tailwind.
story.sentCaption: The open compass face travelled beside Tailwind.

story.title: An old rule at a new angle
story.letter: Cross Bearing sets the compass panels on different corners. Short Rule keeps two upright ruler strips around its narrow opening. Put the upright strips beside the separated compass panels.
story.goal: Make and send Cross Bearing and Short Rule.
story.sentCaption: The compass panels met the familiar ruler strips.

story.title: Room for the wind
story.letter: The kite now carries an open window between its dark sails. Keep that opening beside the compass hinge; neither needs to be filled.
story.goal: Make and send Compass Hinge and Wind Window.
story.sentCaption: The window and hinge left room between them.

story.title: Directions that can stay different
story.letter: One crossing belongs to the compass panels, the other to the kite spar. They do not need to point the same way to close this envelope.
story.goal: Make and send Cross Bearing and Cross Draft.
story.sentCaption: The two crossings finished Cross Currents.

story.title: An opening for a small thought
story.letter: The bottle neck lifts away from its open mouth. The pen from Small Impressions offers an Inkling. Send the two openings, and a parcel will join the table.
story.goal: Make and send Bottle Uncapped and Inkling.
story.sentCaption: The open bottle and the Inkling made room for the parcel.

story.title: The letter already here
story.letter: An Open Letter may still be waiting from an earlier envelope. It belongs beside Bottle Uncapped in this small reply. If you keep the bottle for the parcel instead, this letter will wait.
story.goal: Make and send Bottle Uncapped and Open Letter.
story.sentCaption: The bottle opening reached the Open Letter.

story.title: A corner to keep
story.letter: The parcel makes a deep corner beneath its crossing strap. Put Bottle Uncapped beside it. The same bottle picture may be useful to the other waiting reply, so choose where it goes first.
story.goal: Make and send Parcel Corner and Bottle Uncapped.
story.sentCaption: The parcel corner kept company with the bottle opening.

story.title: A strap and a doorway
story.letter: Loose Strap steps one parcel face forward. Neck and Neck leaves a tall opening under the bottle shoulders. The two pictures make a modest, uneven pair.
story.goal: Make and send Loose Strap and Neck and Neck.
story.sentCaption: The stepped parcel and the bottle doorway were sent.

story.title: A measure for a corner
story.letter: The thimble brings back Tilted, two low dotted panels from the last four envelopes. This time it sits beside the parcel corner. There is no packing to get right.
story.goal: Make and send Parcel Corner and Tilted.
story.sentCaption: The familiar little measure found the parcel corner.

story.title: Enough room for now
story.letter: The bottle leaves a doorway; the parcel makes a corner. These small forms are enough to finish Safe Keeping. Their larger pictures remain yours to discover whenever you want.
story.goal: Make and send Neck and Neck and Parcel Corner.
story.sentCaption: The doorway and corner closed Safe Keeping.

story.title: Unequal company
story.letter: One pan hangs lower, and one magnet arm reaches higher. Give these unequal shapes a first reply without asking them to settle into symmetry.
story.goal: Make and send Unequal Pans and Uneven Pull.
story.sentCaption: The unequal pans and uneven pull arrived together.

story.title: Two balances kept separate
story.letter: Keep two Unequal Pans pictures separate for this letter. Across the Gap spreads the magnet arms beside them. Merging the two balances makes Cross Measure, which belongs to another reply.
story.goal: Make and send 2 separate Unequal Pans pictures and Across the Gap.
story.sentCaption: Two separate balances travelled with the broad magnet gap.

story.title: One measure across
story.letter: Cross Measure changes the balance beam at its center. Uneven Pull keeps one magnet arm short. You can merge a pair of Unequal Pans for this reply, or reserve that pair for the other letter.
story.goal: Make and send Cross Measure and Uneven Pull.
story.sentCaption: The changed beam met the uneven magnet.

story.title: Low pans, tall arm
story.letter: Between Weights lowers the pans beside a bent support. Let the taller magnet arm rise next to that low balance. The larger share of this reply belongs to the scales.
story.goal: Make and send Between Weights and Uneven Pull.
story.sentCaption: The low balance and tall magnet arm made their reply.

story.title: The pull changes sides
story.letter: Close Attraction curves its two ends toward the opening. Give it the small Unequal Pans. This time the longer making belongs to the magnet.
story.goal: Make and send Unequal Pans and Close Attraction.
story.sentCaption: The curved magnet ends travelled with the small balance.

story.title: A space between measures
story.letter: The balance crosses at its beam, and the magnet spreads around a gap. Neither picture has to win. Send the pair and leave this envelope at rest.
story.goal: Make and send Cross Measure and Across the Gap.
story.sentCaption: The crossing and the gap finished Give and Take.

story.title: A first fold on fresh paper
story.letter: The accordion raises one end above the other. A fresh sheet from the typewriter gives its open bellows a quiet beginning. A trumpet follows this first reply.
story.goal: Make and send Open Bellows and Paper.
story.sentCaption: The open bellows reached the fresh sheet.

story.title: A turn before the next phrase
story.letter: Off Key turns its key end across the table. Upbeat Brass lifts the trumpet bell. Keep this first duet compact before opening the two longer replies.
story.goal: Make and send Off Key and Upbeat Brass.
story.sentCaption: The turned keys and lifted bell began their duet.

story.title: A call toward the folds
story.letter: Call Back Brass turns the bell over its loop. Open Bellows holds the simpler accordion shape beside it. Keep an accordion picture here if this is the reply you want to finish first.
story.goal: Make and send Open Bellows and Call Back Brass.
story.sentCaption: The returning bell met the open folds.

story.title: The other part of the duet
story.letter: Counterpart draws the accordion ends around a wide opening. Roundabout Brass carries its valves beneath the pipe. This reply spends more paper on the accordion than the other waiting letter does.
story.goal: Make and send Counterpart and Roundabout Brass.
story.sentCaption: The open accordion and the low valves sent their part.

story.title: A familiar ridge in the map
story.letter: The old map brings back River Ridge, with two unequal peaks interrupting its river. Set Off Key beside it for a shorter reply between the larger pictures. The turned keys can keep the map peaks company.
story.goal: Make and send Off Key and River Ridge.
story.sentCaption: The keys and the map ridge took the shorter route.

story.title: A note to keep
story.letter: The trumpet turns upright around its long open loop. Its bell is high, its valves run down the side, and the mouthpiece stays near the table. Make A Note Kept for this one final picture.
story.goal: Make and send A Note Kept.
story.sentCaption: A Note Kept has been sent. There is one small reply left.

story.title: A small reply after the last note
story.letter: Return to the open bellows and the lifted bell. There is no louder ending to make. Send this small pair, then keep the table and all the pictures you have found.
story.goal: Make and send Open Bellows and Upbeat Brass.
story.sentCaption: The small duet closed these four correspondences.

cross-currents.title: Cross Currents

cross-currents.ending: Cross Currents is complete. The compass and kite may keep their different directions. Safe Keeping brings smaller shapes when you want another envelope.
cross-currents.goal: Send every story letter in Cross Currents. Supplies are free; purchases and optional discoveries are not required.

cross-currents.pacingPattern: one short shared introduction, two effort-asymmetric branches, callbacks earned separately, join
